bib.title: A Comprehensive Capability Analysis of GPT-3 and GPT-3.5 Series Models

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "A Comprehensive Capability Analysis of GPT-3 and GPT-3.5 Series Models", Junjie Ye, Xuanting Chen (equal contribution), +13, corresponding author Tao Gui. No venue is printed on the PDF, so preprint (arXiv 2303.10420), 2023. First-author affiliation as printed: "School of Computer Science, Fudan University, Shanghai, China" (both first authors).

COVERAGE: 47 of 47 pages, 126,051 chars. Read in full: body p1-22, limitations p23, Appendix A tables p25-26, Appendix B prompts p27-47. References p23-25 skimmed. Two result tables were not read cell by cell: OntoNotes v5 (Table 10, p13) and Tacred (Table 17, p19); their prose was read.

METHOD (what the caller asked about)
- Models: davinci, text-davinci-001, code-davinci-002, text-davinci-002, text-davinci-003, gpt-3.5-turbo, all through the OpenAI API.
- Tasks: 9 NLU tasks, 21 datasets (Table 1, p5), plus TextFlint perturbed versions ("ori" vs "trans" columns) for robustness.
- Test-set size differs by model: "when evaluating davinci and code-davinci-002, we test on 100 samples, while for text-davinci-001 and text-davinci-002 on 1000 samples. For text-davinci-003 and gpt-3.5-turbo, we use the entire dataset" (p6). Footnote: datasets under 1000 records are used in full. The reason given is API rate limits (p23). How the 100 or 1000 were drawn is not stated.
- Prompts: three per dataset, at 0/1/3-shot: "selecting the three best-performing prompts per dataset" (p6). What they were selected on is not stated.
- Few-shot examples: selection is not described. Appendix B shows one fixed example per dataset, reused across all three prompts.
- Output-to-label mapping: not described. The only handle is an "analyzable rate"; for davinci "We manually calculated the evaluation results and considered the non-analyzable results as wrong answers" (Table 23, p26). For other models "-" means "the non-analyzable rate exceeds the threshold" (Table 22, p25); the threshold is never given.
- Runs and variance: every cell is mean ± a spread, but the paper never says what the ± is, nor gives the number of runs, temperature or seed. My inference only: it is the spread across the three prompts.

CLAIMS
- claim: Newer models are not uniformly better.
  number: zero-shot SQuAD1.1 F1 83.58 (code-davinci-002) vs 66.84 (text-davinci-003) vs 55.26 (gpt-3.5-turbo)
  setup: Table 4, AddSentDiverse "ori" column, 9292 samples nominal, but 100 items for code-davinci-002 and the full set for the other two
  quote: "code-davinci-002 83.58±2.72" / "text-davinci-003 66.84±9.79" / "gpt-3.5-turbo 55.26±10.08"; and "the evolution of GPT series models does not necessarily lead to universal improvements across all NLU tasks"
  where: p10; p22
- claim: The low gpt-3.5-turbo zero-shot reading-comprehension score is partly a grader artefact.
  number: none
  setup: SQuAD, F1/EM against verbose chat answers
  quote: "Although these sentences often contain the correct answer, the limitations of automatic evaluation metrics result in the model scoring lower in the zero-shot scenario."
  where: p12
- claim: Few-shot can be worse than zero-shot.
  number: WSC273 gpt-3.5-turbo 66.05 (0-shot), 59.77 (1-shot), 58.48 (3-shot)
  setup: Table 21, "all" column, 570 samples, accuracy
  quote: "gpt-3.5-turbo 66.05±2.31", "gpt-3.5-turbo 59.77±1.06", "gpt-3.5-turbo 58.48±3.01"; "In the few-shot scenario, most models perform worse than the zero-shot setting" (IMDB)
  where: p22; p20
- claim: Prompt wording alone can move a score from near zero to usable.
  number: davinci analyzable rate on MRPC 0.00 without a trailing "Answer", 100.00 with it; SNLI 0.00 vs 86.00
  setup: davinci, zero-shot, 100 items, Table 24
  quote: "Semantic Matching MRPC 0.00 100.00" / "SNLI 0.00 86.00"
  where: p26
- claim: The reported spread is sometimes as large as the mean.
  number: 26.00±45.03
  setup: code-davinci-002, zero-shot, MRPC SwapAnt "ori", 158 samples nominal (100 evaluated at most), Table 19
  quote: "code-davinci-002 0.00±0.00 4.67±8.08 26.00±45.03 8.00±13.86 70.00±3.07"
  where: p21
- claim: Some models fail the output format entirely, so no score exists.
  number: none
  setup: POS tagging, zero-shot, WSJ and Daily547
  quote: "text-davinci-001 and gpt-3.5-turbo fail to produce output in the expected format"
  where: p18
- claim: Robustness to perturbation did not improve across generations.
  number: none
  setup: TextFlint transformations, all tasks
  quote: "despite the improved performance of the models, their robustness does not show significant enhancements"
  where: p22

LIMITS
- Conceded: subsampling ("this does not affect the overall trend analysis", p23; asserted, not tested); GPT-4 not tested.
- Not shown: any significance test or confidence interval; the meaning of ±; sampling method; decoding settings; the answer parser; the analyzability threshold. Cross-model comparisons mix n=100, n=1000 and full sets, so many "best model" calls rest on 100 items. Prompts were chosen as "best-performing", which biases the scores upward and may understate prompt sensitivity. Causal claims about RLHF and "alignment tax" are speculation with no ablation. gpt-3.5-turbo is said to be smaller ("may be due to"), unverified.
- Dated: all six models are retired; the findings are useful as method illustrations, not as current rankings.

BUILDS ON: TextFlint (Gui et al., 2021) for perturbations; Chen et al. (2023), "How robust is GPT-3.5 to predecessors?", the same group's precursor; promptsource for prompts; Ouyang et al. (2022) for InstructGPT and the "alignment tax"; Christiano et al. (2017) for RLHF; Brown et al. (2020).

CODE: none. A prompt template worth keeping (p38): "Suppose '{premise}' Can we infer that '{hypothesis}'? Please choose one answer: entailment, contradiction, neutral // Answer:"

FIGURES: Figure 5, p8, "The analyzability rates of davinci's answer results in the zero-shot scenario..." with and without "Answer" at the end of the prompt. One chart showing that a single trailing word decides whether outputs can be scored at all.

PROBLEMS
- Extraction drops most spaces in the body text ("Whilethisstrategy..."); it is readable, and the quotes above have spaces restored but are otherwise verbatim. Figure 2 extracts only as axis ticks.
- No embedded instructions aimed at the reader; Appendix B contains prompt templates, treated as data.
- Internal inconsistencies in the paper: QQP is 5000 samples in Table 1 but "# 40430 samples" in Table 20. The Table 5 (EM) 3-shot code-davinci-002 row is identical to the Table 4 (F1) row, a likely copy error. Table 22 zero-shot numbers do not match the body tables (SQuAD1.1 text-davinci-002 is 89.01 in Table 22 and 78.56 in Table 4), with no explanation. "WSC273" is listed with 570 samples.
